title: Midweek latency signal report + handoff notes (2028-11-03)
content:
Summary:

This midweek note captures a transient tail-latency signal observed after the 2028-11-03 morning canary for model v2.8-q4. The event produced short P99 spikes (~750ms -> 2.1s) in the hosted-api region-us-west for ~18 minutes. No user-facing error rates were reported, but internal SLO margin decreased and a brief alert flap occurred.

High-level timeline (local times):
- 2028-11-03 09:03: roll-forward: canary deploy v2.8-q4 to 5% traffic (auto canary pipeline).
- 2028-11-03 09:09: observability flagged rising 1m P99 (from baseline 0.75s to ~1.6s) on route /api/generate in us-west.
- 2028-11-03 09:12: alerts fired (p99>1.5s, sustained 2 windows). On-call paged (primary: Liam Chen).
- 2028-11-03 09:15: initial mitigations applied: reduce burst_scale to 0.8, increase autoscale minimum workers +2 for region us-west.
- 2028-11-03 09:19: rollback initiated to v2.7-quant (previous stable variant) at 5% traffic.
- 2028-11-03 09:27: traffic normalized; p99 declined to baseline by 09:31.
- 2028-11-03 09:40: incident closed (post-handoff) pending RCA and follow-ups.

Incident notes (observations):
- The spike correlated closely with the canary window for v2.8-q4 and with higher-than-usual batch sizes on requests routed to that variant.
- KV-cache hit ratio dropped ~14% during the spike window for hot prefixes that v2.8-q4 requests used.
- Kernel selection logs show that a new heuristic path (matrix_scheduling_v3) was selected for several worker hosts where sequence-length distribution was slightly above typical. Those hosts showed disproportionate p99 increase.
- No memory pressure nor OOMs were reported. CPU on affected GPUs increased by ~10–12% compared to baseline.
- Autoscale reacted but minimum pool size prevented more immediate capacity shift; the early burst_scale tweak helped, but rollback to v2.7-quant resolved the tail latency faster.

Immediate impact to SLOs:
- Rolling 24h SLO (p99 <= 1.2s) had one 5-minute breach window during the event; our alerting threshold is intentionally conservative and produced a page (expected).
- Cost impact negligible (short duration), but stability margin reduced for the rest of the day for the affected route.

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
1) Model variant v2.8-q4 uses a kernel scheduling heuristic (matrix_scheduling_v3) that, for slightly longer sequence-lengths and the changed token emission distribution in this canary, increases the effective batch latency for tail requests when paired with lower KV-cache hit rates.
2) Canary traffic had a subtle prefix distribution change (experiment row — a/b test traffic row) that exacerbated cache churn on a subset of hosts.
3) Autoscaler configuration has a min_worker floor that delays reactive scaling for short-duration spikes; burst_scale is needed but not always tuned for new heuristics.

What we checked (quick):
- Host-level logs around 09:00–09:30 for affected IPs (no disk, no OOM).
- KV-cache metrics and prefix heatmap (confirmed hit ratio drop).
- Kernel selection traces (matrix_scheduling_v3 chosen on affected hosts).
- Canary traffic routing (fractions and experiment tags) to ensure traffic weighting behaved as expected.

Mitigation and action items (owner, ETA):
- Short term: add a safety throttle in canary pipeline to limit concurrency per host for new scheduling heuristics. (Owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2028-11-07)
- Short term: add automatic rollback trigger when p99 > 1.5s sustained for 2 consecutive 1m windows in canary. (Owner: Ava Patel, ETA: 2028-11-06)
- Medium term: add kernel selection telemetry to model-profile dashboard and a per-variant "heuristic risk" tag that the canary-runner uses. (Owner: Sofia Martinez, ETA: 2028-11-20)
- Medium term: instrument KV-cache prefix churn signal so canary runner can surface low hit-ratio anomalies early. (Owner: Daniel Kim, ETA: 2028-11-17)
- Long term: evaluate/simulate batch-latency for matrix_scheduling_v3 with synthetic prefixes (bench harness). Feed results to compilation/kernelselector tuning. (Owner: Research/Applied-ML, ETA: 2028-12-05)

On-call handoff (what follow-up is required for next shift):
- Monitor the canary job for v2.8-q4 re-deploy attempts (do not re-enable without the safety throttle or explicit sign-off).
- Watch the p99 and KV-cache hit alerts for /api/generate in us-west; escalate to perf-eng if a second breach occurs.
- Review the PR linked below that attempted the heuristic change (PR: infra#3412).
- Check for any rolled-back canary re-runs from feature flags dashboard.

Meeting sync items (this week):
- Friday perf sync: present quickbench results and kernel telemetry proposal (Sofia lead).
- Canary-runner triage: add rollback-trigger proposal to pipeline backlog (Ava).

Observability notes & proposed tweaks:
- Current p99 alert uses a static threshold that may be too tight for canaries during hardware/kernel experimentation. Propose separate canary-sensitive thresholds that trigger non-pager first (ops-prefix).
- Add a short-lived annotation on canary traces that captures variant kernel selection and batch size; this will help correlate traces without digging through host logs.
- Quick dashboard: new panel showing KV-cache prefix heatmap overlaid with variant traffic fraction — helps spot prefix churn during canaries.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is matrix_scheduling_v3 benefiting typical production requests or just edge-case long sequences? If not beneficial, consider disabling for the variant family until proven.
- Should we add a "fast-signal checkpoint" in canary rollout to sample KV-cache metrics at 30s cadence (trade-off: extra metric pressure)?
- We saw higher GPU CPU utilization but not dramatic; what micro-ops are more expensive in matrix_scheduling_v3? (ask applied-ml for kernel trace walk-through).

Quick wins (low effort):
- Lower the canary default concurrency limit from 64 -> 48 for new kernel heuristics (reduces host-level batch growth). (ETA: 2028-11-04)
- Add non-pager alert for KV-cache hit ratio drop >10% for 1m in canary windows (ETA: 2028-11-06)

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3412
- Incident ticket: SRE-4783
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01AB2CD3/p1730009876543
- Canary run: pipeline-id: canary-2028-11-03-0910 (internal dashboard)

Sign-off / next update:
- I will update this doc after the Friday perf sync with decisions on kernel telemetry and canary pipeline changes. Leaving this as an "in_review" handoff for the weekend on-call.

-- Ava (notes left in quick bullet style to be fleshed out after perf sync)
